description: We are a passionate team of young innovators combining software development, data analysis, research, and creative problem-solving to build Cosmos Care, while being eager to learn and grow together.
summary: Jarvis is an AI system that combines the use of localized LLMs into an easy-to-use vitals and solar radiation monitoring system. Our research revealed that astronauts throughout space missions have always been ridiculously close to Acute Radiation Syndrome (ARS), astronauts consumed about 20% less calories than required to maintain their bone and muscle densities and lastly astronauts face isolation in longer trips. These issues are all resolved by our project, a visual system that specializes in warning astronauts about incoming solar storms. In addition to providing statistics on solar storms, our system constantly monitors the status of an astronaut’s vital organs. The organs that are monitored include heart rate, brain activity, the air pressure of lungs and the temperature of an astronaut’s skin. These are shown due to their direct correlation with the organs first affected by ARS. We also have a system that monitors the food intake of astronauts by analyzing the quality of crops they consume. This allows the astronauts to consume the maximum amount of nutrition whilst eating less food. Lastly our system provides its users with an AI companion which is locally hosted to prevent isolation. These are all implementations that provide astronauts with life saving statistics and help them to monitor their health.
details:
JARVIS is an integrated health and environmental monitoring software designed to safeguard the physical and psychological well-being of astronauts during deep-space missions.

Core Functions

Astronaut Health Tracking: Monitors real-time vital signs and physical biomarkers to detect medical anomalies early.

Predictive Radiation Forecasting: Anticipates dangerous solar radiation events so crews can take immediate shielding measures.

Psychological Support: Features a specialized space journal designed to combat isolation, confinement, and space loneliness.

How does our project work?

Radiation: Jarvis reads live proton data from the GOES satellites every 5 minutes, plus NASA DONKI solar-event alerts. Our machine-learning model forecasts the chance of a radiation storm and explains why. When the alert level rises, the system guides the crew to shelter.

Vitals: a 3D body view shows the readings for the brain, heart and lungs, and flags anything outside the astronaut’s normal range.

Garden: a camera image of a plant’s leaves is checked to spot unhealthy crops early.

Mind: a private journal and an AI companion that runs locally (Llama 3.2 through Ollama), so nothing needs the internet.

Voice: “Hey Jarvis” works hands-free. The wake word and speech-to-text run on the device (openWakeWord, Whisper).

JARVIS enhances deep-space missions by transforming reactive medical responses into proactive protection. By continuously tracking real-time vital signs, it detects physical anomalies early, preventing minor health issues from becoming mission-critical emergencies. Its predictive radiation forecasting gives astronauts vital lead time to deploy shielding against dangerous solar events. Beyond physical safety, the integrated space journal builds psychological resilience, actively combating the severe isolation and loneliness of long-duration spaceflight. Additionally, we have developed a system that tracks the health of plants since many researches proved that plants helps astronauts to cope with space loneliness. Ultimately, this unified approach maximizes crew endurance, improves decision-making under stress, and significantly increases the overall safety and success rate of deep-space exploration.

Our mission is to develop an advanced health support system that prioritizes and safeguards astronaut well-being, delivering a superior standard of care that honors their dedication and surpasses existing aerospace standards.
